lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
- Cut the signal's daily turnover from 34% to 21% with a cost-aware position smoother, keeping 90% of gross returns and lowering estimated slippage by a third.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Documented the backtest assumptions, transaction-cost model and known failure regimes in the desk's research wiki, which the next intern cohort used to onboard in their first week.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Built the lab's simulation pipeline on the shared cluster, cutting a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours, with every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator that tightens the previous bound by a log factor; it is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Placed 41st of 2,900 teams with a gradient-boosting ensemble on 300 engineered features, finishing in the top 2% of the private leaderboard.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Wrote the team's feature-selection script using permutation importance, trimming 900 candidate features to 300 without losing validation score.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch
Methods: time-series econometrics, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Clarify scope and ownership of accomplishments.
items.because: Several claims sound larger than what a three-month internship could independently accomplish.

items.says: Make results more technically precise.
items.because: Define metrics, baselines, time periods, and whether results are yours or the team’s.

items.says: Reduce lower-value detail, especially documentation/implementation bullets.
items.because: Some bullets emphasize documentation or implementation without showing enough research impact.

items.says: Improve targeting by emphasizing most relevant skills and research interests for the target role.
items.because: For quant research roles, technical skills and research interests should be more prominent; for academic roles, emphasize publications, presentations, teaching, and mathematical/statistical contributions.

items.says: Add missing context such as dissertation topic/advisor, publications, and possibly relevant coursework.
items.because: You should include dissertation topic/advisor, publications or working papers, and possibly relevant coursework if applying before graduation.

items.says: Replace portfolio link with a real, directly relevant portfolio link.
items.because: Make sure it leads to useful public work rather than only a profile page.

items.says: Include only links that materially strengthen your application; avoid a long list of weak links.
Specify subfield or research area if relevant to target roles.
Add dissertation topic, advisor, or research interests if they strengthen candidacy.
items.because: Resume shows projects but not central doctoral research.

items.says: Add GPA only if exceptional and expected in your target market.
Ensure expected graduation date is current.
items.because: A stale date can make the resume look neglected.

items.says: Add relevant concentration, honors, or distinction if applicable.
Add relevant coursework only if applying to roles where it compensates for limited experience.
items.because: Given the strength of your experience, coursework is probably lower priority.

items.says: Add asset class, strategy type, or desk scope if it can be disclosed and helps recruiters understand context.
Distinguish between work you personally implemented, analysis you contributed to, and outcomes achieved by the broader desk or team.
items.because: Because the internship is short, bullets should clarify your role.

items.says: If applying before the internship has ended, change tense consistently and avoid presenting future outcomes as completed.
Clarify whether Sharpe improvement applies to new signal alone, desk book after incorporating the signal, or a hypothetical portfolio combination.
items.because: 'Desk book' currently makes the attribution ambiguous.

items.says: Identify the comparison point: prior strategy, prior book, or a version without the signal.
State whether Sharpe is annualized and whether it is net of all relevant costs, financing, and market-impact assumptions.
Explain the 18-month period and why it is appropriate.
items.because: Readers need to know whether it overlaps with the six years mentioned later.

items.says: Avoid implying you alone raised the desk’s live or realized Sharpe unless that is literally defensible.
Clarify what 'daily turnover' means and whether it is measured at the signal, strategy, or portfolio level.
Explain what 'keeping 90% of gross returns' is relative to: the unsmoothed signal, the original strategy, or another benchmark.
'Lowering estimated slippage by a third' should specify the comparison basis and whether it is modeled or observed.
Consider whether this bullet duplicates the first bullet’s performance discussion.
items.because: If space is limited, prioritize the bullet that better demonstrates your individual contribution and technical sophistication.

items.says: Explain what was purged and what the embargo protected against, either here or in an interview.
items.because: Current wording assumes the reader understands specialized terms.

items.says: Clarify whether the six years includes the 18-month evaluation period in the first bullet and how the periods were divided.
'Every backtest decision used only information available at the time' is a strong claim; retain it only if you can defend it for all aspects, not just train/test split.
Consider adding the number of folds or evaluation windows if space permits and if it demonstrates rigor.
Clarify whether you designed the feature store, implemented it, or contributed to an existing system.
Add the technical environment if relevant and not already covered elsewhere.
'Reused in two later signal projects' would be stronger if the projects’ importance or the team’s usage were clearer.
Make sure 'point-in-time joins' is accurate and includes corrections for data revisions, corporate actions, symbol changes, and availability timestamps where relevant.
Clarify whether portfolio managers approved a live allocation because of your analysis or as part of a broader team process.
'For the next quarter' is somewhat vague; if the allocation actually occurred, include the outcome; if only approved, preserve that distinction.
Keep this bullet only if the role emphasizes research governance, reproducibility, or team enablement.
items.because: This is the weakest Northpeak bullet in terms of space efficiency.

items.says: Emphasize the value of the documentation: reproducibility, reviewability, compliance, or reduced ramp-up time.
items.because: Do not include all of these unless true.

items.says: Consider whether 'Research Assistant' understates your work if you had substantial independent research responsibility.
Add the faculty supervisor or lab name only if it is recognizable and useful.
If the lab work resulted in publications, presentations, or software used outside the lab, connect those outputs more explicitly.
Clarify the computing environment if it matters: cluster type, parallelization framework, or scheduler.
Add whether the study produced the same statistical output or whether the speedup came from changed methodology.
Make sure 'every run reproducible from its seed and configuration file' also covers package versions, data versions, and environment specification if you intend it to mean fully reproducible.
Consider whether the 2,000-run study was yours or the lab’s; make ownership clear.
Specify what 'tightens the previous bound by a log factor' means mathematically if the target audience is technical.
items.because: As written, it is impressive but somewhat opaque.

items.says: Identify your authorship status and the paper’s status more clearly elsewhere in the resume.
items.because: A paper should not be buried under an assistantship if it is a significant research output.

items.says: Avoid overstating the result if the improvement depends on additional assumptions or a narrower setting than the prior bound.
Clarify whether the 4.8/5 rating came from a formal university evaluation and indicate the response count if available and meaningful.
Teaching responsibilities should be framed around scope and quality rather than only quantity.
Add a repository or package link if the package is public and maintained.
Clarify whether the download count is from CRAN, GitHub, or another source, and whether it includes automated downloads if that matters.
Explain your role in design, implementation, maintenance, or documentation.
Consider whether 'Independent Research' is the best label if it is also part of your dissertation or supervised work; be consistent about ownership.
Indicate the current status accurately: working paper, manuscript, public code, or ongoing analysis.
items.because: Since it has been ongoing for a long time.

items.says: Add the data frequency, forecast horizon, and evaluation period somewhere in the project section.
items.because: Without them, the result is difficult to assess.

items.says: Avoid presenting this as fully complete if the study is still changing.
Clarify whether the 7% is an average, median, pooled, or aggregate improvement across the 30 indices.
State the out-of-sample period and forecast horizon.
Explain whether the model comparison used the same information set, tuning budget, and data treatment.
Specify whether the 30 equity indices are country indices, broad-market indices, or another universe if that affects interpretation.
Mention computational or modeling techniques only if they distinguish the work from ordinary deep-learning experimentation.
Clarify how the 24-of-30 result relates to the 7% aggregate improvement.
items.because: Readers may otherwise interpret it as a separate success metric.

items.says: State whether the crisis periods were pre-specified and identify them if relevant.
Be precise about the testing setup: one-sided or two-sided tests, loss differential definition, and treatment of dependence.
items.because: The listed claim should be defensible.

items.says: 'Held at the 5% level' should be used only if the multiple-testing procedure and test direction support that wording.
Add a link if the paper or presentation materials are public.
The page count is less important than the paper’s status and audience; prioritize whether it is a working paper, submitted paper, or publicly available research.
Make sure the paper’s authorship and supervision are clear if it was not solely yours.
Add the competition name and organizer if it is recognizable and publicly verifiable.
Identify your individual contribution more clearly, since 'Team of 3' means the results cannot automatically be attributed to you.
If the competition data or target is unrelated to finance, explain its relevance through the methods rather than relying on the title.
Confirm that 'private leaderboard' and 'top 2%' are consistent; use one primary measure if space is limited.
Clarify whether the final rank was based on a single submission or a team submission.
'300 engineered features' is less valuable than the modeling choices, validation design, or your specific contribution; keep it only if feature construction was a meaningful part of your work.
Avoid making this look like a stronger signal of production readiness than it is; competition performance is not the same as deployable research.
Clarify whether the 0.02 gap was an absolute score difference and whether closing the gap improved the final result or only made validation more realistic.
Explain what was grouped by time and why the original folds were inappropriate.

Be careful with the phrase 'validation leakage.' If the original setup was merely misaligned with the competition structure rather than truly leaking future information, use technically accurate terminology.
Clarify whether permutation importance was computed in a leakage-safe way and on which validation scheme.
Explain why reducing features mattered: speed, stability, interpretability, or generalization.
'Without losing validation score' is a weak outcome by itself and may invite concern about overfitting to validation; pair it with evidence from the leaderboard or repeated time splits if available.
Make sure the number of candidates is consistent with the preceding bullet and that the reduction was not performed using information unavailable during the competition.
Add important tools that are genuinely relevant to your target roles, such as SQL, C++, Git, Linux, distributed computing, or specific numerical libraries.
Separate programming languages from frameworks and tools if you have enough items to justify the distinction.
Include proficiency levels only if they are meaningful and defensible; avoid vague labels such as 'advanced.'
For quant roles, omitting SQL or C++ can be noticeable if you use them or are expected to use them.
Organize methods around the roles you are targeting.
Add methods clearly demonstrated elsewhere in the resume, such as market microstructure, volatility modeling, statistical learning theory, purged cross-validation, or transaction-cost modeling.
Avoid listing methods that appear nowhere in your experience or projects.
'Gradient boosting' is a model family, while the other items are broader research areas; consider making the categories more consistent.
Add relevant mathematical foundations only if you have space and can support them through coursework or research.
Add a publications and working papers section, especially because you have a paper under review and a substantial volatility study.
items.because: Include publication status accurately and distinguish published, submitted, under review, and unpublished work.

items.says: Add a presentations section or incorporate presentations into relevant entries if you have multiple talks, conference presentations, or seminars.
Add a dissertation or research interests section to explain the connection among your research areas.
items.because: This would help explain the connection among high-dimensional statistics, volatility forecasting, and quantitative research.

items.says: Consider adding relevant tools, databases, cloud platforms, numerical methods, or programming languages that are currently absent.
items.because: Only include technologies you could discuss in detail.

items.says: Keep the resume to one page only if you are applying primarily to industry roles and can preserve the strongest evidence; a two-page resume is reasonable for a Ph.D. candidate with this amount of relevant research.
Use consistent punctuation across bullets.
items.because: Currently, most bullets end with periods; preserve that consistently.

items.says: Avoid line breaks that split a metric or technical phrase awkwardly.
items.because: This is mostly a layout issue, but it affects readability.

items.says: Use standard date formatting throughout.
Make section hierarchy visually clear without excessive design.
Put technical skills somewhere recruiters will see quickly, but do not let the skills section replace evidence from your experience.
Ensure every metric is defensible, defined, and attributable to you.
items.because: The resume’s sophistication will cause technical interviewers to probe the backtest methodology closely.
